hypothesis: A generic profit floor and trailing stop activated before HYPE's eight-hour soft boundary may retain more after-cost profit than the active no-target contract.
decision: Reaffirm rejection of the frozen 25/15/10, 40/15/20, and 60/15/30 bps activation/floor/trail policies. Seven resolved HYPE lifecycles now show that every policy reduced mean after-cost return after normalizing each trade by its own entry notional. Preserve the current exit contract while prospective exit evidence accumulates; do not apply these challengers to the open lifecycle or a future profile.
falsifier: A prospectively frozen pre-soft profit-protection policy that improves actual after-cost exits across multiple non-adjacent profile-matched live windows without increasing loss concentration would update this rejection; changed source-prefix hashes would invalidate the present audit.
limitations: Seven resolved HYPE closes remain sparse and are not independent market samples.
The all-live mechanism sample spans three source profiles and six process runs with differing sizing contracts.
Basis-point normalization removes notional scale but does not construct a counterfactual shared-portfolio equity path.
Completed one-minute bars cannot reconstruct intraminute trigger ordering.
Counterfactual fills reuse each actual exit fill/reference ratio and fee rate rather than submitted orders.
The current v11 HYPE lifecycle is open and excluded from resolved policy comparisons.
